claims.text: The onset of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is governed by localized surface premelting induced by Cu segregation.
Cu has the lowest melting point among Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu.
Heating causes Cu to migrate preferentially toward the nanoparticle surface.
Surface enrichment in Cu lowers the local melting temperature.
A liquid-like surface layer forms first and progressively invades the nanoparticle interior.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and compositionally homogeneous.
Suppressing or enhancing Cu surface segregation under otherwise identical heating conditions provides a controlled test of the proposed mechanism.
An inert atmosphere avoids oxidation during the heating experiment.
A Cu-enriched surface layer acts as a localized liquid-phase mediator that accelerates the overall melting transition.
The Cu-enriched liquid-like surface layer reduces the energy barrier for melting.
Enhanced Cu surface segregation will shift the DSC premelting onset to a lower temperature than in compositionally homogeneous baseline nanoparticles.
In situ TEM will show a liquid-like surface layer before bulk melting in nanoparticles with enhanced Cu surface segregation.
Nanoparticles with a uniform elemental distribution have a higher observable premelting and melting onset temperature than Cu-segregated nanoparticles.
Rapid heating is relevant to high-temperature synthesis of HEA nanoparticles.
Oxidation or markedly different heating rates may alter Cu segregation dynamics.
The relative importance of Cu segregation, defects, and size-dependent melting may vary with nanoparticle size and synthesis history.
Thermal history can affect the properties of HEA nanoparticles.
If minimizing Cu segregation produces no significant change in melting onset, progression, or surface behavior, the claim that Cu segregation governs the transition onset is falsified.
